name: French Quarter
tagline: Iron balconies, courtyards and the loudest six blocks in Louisiana
description: The oldest part of the city is a tight grid of Creole townhouses with wrought iron galleries and hidden courtyards. Bourbon Street carries the noise, while the lower Quarter around Royal and Esplanade stays surprisingly residential. Everything is walkable, and a handful of quiet courtyard cafes make workable morning offices.
bestFor: Short stay nomads who want to live inside the postcard and walk everywhere.
pros: Total walkability with no car needed
Courtyard cafes and coffee shops open early
Streetcar and bus lines at the edges
cons: Nightly noise from Bourbon Street bleeds for blocks
Highest nightly rates in the city
Petty theft and aggressive panhandling after dark

name: Marigny and Bywater
tagline: Frenchmen Street jazz backed by pastel shotgun houses
description: Just downriver of the Quarter, Faubourg Marigny gives you Frenchmen Street live music every night, and Bywater behind it is rows of brightly painted shotgun houses, artist studios and Crescent Park along the river levee. The crowd skews younger, queerer and more creative than anywhere else in town.
bestFor: Creatives and musicians who want real local nightlife without Bourbon Street.
pros: Frenchmen Street music without the tourist crush
Crescent Park riverfront for running and cycling
Strong cafe and independent bar scene
cons: Bywater streets are dark and thinly patrolled at night
Rapid short term rental growth has pushed rents up
Low lying blocks flood in heavy summer storms

name: Garden District
tagline: Antebellum mansions under live oaks on the streetcar line
description: Broad blocks of Greek Revival and Italianate mansions sit behind cast iron fences and enormous live oaks, with Magazine Street running along the edge as a long strip of boutiques, coffee shops and restaurants. Lafayette Cemetery anchors the centre. It is quiet, green and mostly settled residents rather than students.
bestFor: Nomads on longer stays who want calm streets and a walkable Magazine Street.
pros: St Charles streetcar straight into downtown
Magazine Street shops and cafes on foot
Some of the highest, driest ground in the city
cons: Expensive rents for the space you get
Tour groups walk the blocks daily
Nightlife is limited, you commute for it

name: Mid-City
tagline: Bayou St John, City Park and the best value in town
description: Centred on the Canal Street streetcar and the slow water of Bayou St John, Mid-City is doubles and shotgun houses, neighbourhood po-boy shops and the 1,300 acre City Park at its northern edge. Rents drop noticeably compared with anywhere near the Quarter, and the crowd is locals and families.
bestFor: Budget conscious nomads staying a month or more who want space and greenery.
pros: Clearly cheaper rents than the Quarter or Uptown
City Park and the bayou for running and paddling
cons: Several blocks flood badly in heavy rain
Car or bike strongly recommended for errands
Coffee shop options thin out away from the streetcar

name: Uptown and Freret
tagline: University oaks, porch culture and a walkable food strip
description: Wrapped around Tulane and Loyola, Uptown is grand oak lined avenues and student doubles in equal measure, with Freret Street as the compact food and bar strip in the middle. Audubon Park sits on the river side. Term time fills it with students, summers empty it out and rents soften.
bestFor: Nomads who want quiet weekday work with cafes, parks and a university crowd nearby.
pros: Audubon Park and the river levee for exercise
Freret and Magazine strips for food and coworking cafes
Elevated ground that drains better than most areas
cons: Student party noise on weekends near campus
Long streetcar ride to downtown, roughly 30 minutes
Armed robbery reports cluster near campus edges at night
